headline: No 64–68 water anywhere — the break has slid off the triangle
body:
Safety first: a small craft advisory covers the outer waters from Point Sal to Santa Cruz Island, including Santa Rosa, from late tonight through Saturday morning, with NW 15–25 kt and 6–9 ft Friday. That writes off Santa Rosa Flats; its own point forecast is already 5.1 ft today. Inside the channel it's mild — today SE 5–15 kt backing west, 2–3 ft, and 3.4 ft at the triangle's middle. Friday looks similar, light early, W 10–15 kt by afternoon, 3.3 ft, with the hurricane swells beginning to fill in.

The honest call: neither day is a bluefin day on temperature. Nothing in the data comes near the 64–68 band. The triangle's corners read 71.6 west, 71.8 east, and 69.8 at the south point in the Santa Cruz Basin (70.2 Friday) — the break has slid off the zone entirely, and the far grounds are warmer still, Osborn's SW flank 73.2 and San Nicolas 71.4. If you go, go today and work the south point for the coolest edge and bait. Skip the 68-nm run.
